decisions.reason: Although later website visibility is weak, this loader line is close to the firm's underground core, so shared engineering, service capabilities and some organizational slack make continued retention more likely unless performance clearly falls below aspiration.

The mining truck line is related to the core business but its lack of later visibility suggests weaker-than-aspired acceptance, so management would likely reallocate resources if it has not built enough scale by now.
A construction site dumper is more exposed to competitive, less distinctive segments than the firm's main niches, so uncertain results would likely trigger problemistic search and withdrawal.

This inclined furniture lift line fits the firm's lifting and service-oriented capabilities, and with no clear evidence of failure boundedly rational management would likely continue it while learning accumulates.

The inclined building material lift line matches the firm's construction and material-handling strengths well, so aspiration levels are more likely to be met or at least tolerated during continued market development.
As a narrower truck-mounted variant, it likely has higher complexity and lower volume than the broader lift lines, making it a more plausible candidate for exit if returns remain uncertain.
